## OPR-001 — operator field report: "presets load, sliders do not change the synth"

Traced on f030926, in the operator's own order. All four named mechanisms are clean:

1. Control → engine — `plugin/ui/FaderCell.cpp:157-180` `userMoved()` → `engine.setValue (baseCc, v)`;

   one engine. `updating` is cleared at the end of `userMoved` (`:221`), so no stuck guard.
2. Engine → emit — `plugin/cc/CCEngine.cpp:61-82`: guards only `isPositiveAndBelow(cc,128)` and

   (`:114-121`) bails only on `!emitEnabled || sink == nullptr`; `emitEnabled` defaults true
   (`CCEngine.h:113`) and is set true at `plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:127`. No learn/takeover gate.
3. Message shape — sink at `plugin/PluginProcessor.cpp:112-125` forwards
   `getRawData()/getRawDataSize()` of `MidiMessage::controllerEvent` = `{0xB0|(ch-1), cc, value}`.
4. Port — `midi/MidiPort.mm:453-459` → `bytesNeeded(0xB0)==2` → `Impl::send(bytes,3)` → `MIDISend`,
   the **same** `Impl::send` `sendSysEx` uses (`:447-452`), so "presets load" proves it reaches the unit.

Remaining asymmetry (not a code defect, and the only thing left that matches the symptom): CC is
channel-addressed, SysEx is not. `emitCc` sends on `midiChannel == 0 ? 1 : midiChannel`, and
`midiChannel` is set only by `CCEngine::setState` (`plugin/cc/CCEngine.cpp:352`) — the editor has no
channel control. Settle it by reading `midiChannel` from the session's engine state XML and by
watching a MIDI monitor on the Nymphes output while a fader moves.

Defect found while tracing, fixed: the sink discarded `MidiPort::sendChannel`'s `bool`, so a refused
CC was silent. Before (f030926 + my earlier queue fix):

    const juce::SpinLock::ScopedLockType lock (ccOutLock);
    for (int i = 0; i < ccOutCount; ++i) { midi.sendChannel (p[0], p[1], p[2]); }   // bool dropped
    ccOutCount = 0;

After:

    std::array<std::uint8_t, kCcOutCapacity*3> batch {}; int count = 0;
    { const juce::SpinLock::ScopedLockType lock (ccOutLock); count = ccOutCount; batch = ccOut; ccOutCount = 0; }
    for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i)
        if (midi.sendChannel (p[0], p[1], p[2])) ccSendFailureReported = false;
        else if (! ccSendFailureReported) { ccSendFailureReported = true; setError ("A CC could not be sent (is the Nymphes port still open?). ..."); }

The batch is now copied out of the spin lock before sending, so `Impl::send`'s `std::vector` allocation
and MIDI-server call happen with the lock released.

    100% tests passed out of 7                        (ccmap, cli_smoke, codec_text, params_gen,

Cross-reference: `plugin/ui/CcStrip.*` is never constructed in the tree (`grep "new CcStrip"` finds
only its own constructor), so that component's slider path (`CcStrip.cpp:127-137`) is dead UI.

therefore only probes `labelFor()` inside/outside each declared range, which is safe, and
confirms each discrete entry resolves its min and max while continuous entries have no
labels. (The table also differs from `midi/CCMap.h` on CC 19/25 discreteness - that is the
